financials_interim.notes: Same source as GROUP row (source_id 52487), STATEMENT OF FINANCIAL POSITION - COMPANY (doc p.3), STATEMENT OF PROFIT OR LOSS - COMPANY (doc p.5), STATEMENT OF CASH FLOW - COMPANY (doc p.9) -- HPWR's standalone parent, which holds Investments in subsidiaries of 1,878,171,059 (unchanged QoQ) rather than consolidating them; the parent directly owns/operates only a subset of plant capacity (see GROUP row's segment note for the consolidated Hydro/Solar segment breakdown, which is not separately available at Company level). See GROUP row's notes for the shared FX-disclosure gap, hydrology-disclosure gap, and inferred share sub-division/EPS-restatement explanation (all apply identically at Company level; shares_in_issue is the same single listed share count, 430,924,135). Revenue fell 33% (73,142,473 vs 109,272,972 PY); Gross profit fell 40% (52,407,605 vs 86,776,401); Results from operating activities fell 56% (28,532,764 vs 64,160,284, also losing the 516,502 PY Other operating income which did not recur). Finance cost rose 30% (62,732,695 vs 48,338,342, a Rs14.39Mn increase) while Finance income rose sharply (5,891,999 vs 226,696 PY) -- net effect: Profit before tax SWUNG FROM A PROFIT TO A LOSS, (28,307,933) vs +16,048,638 PY (-276%), i.e. the 30% finance-cost increase combined with the 56% operating decline was enough on its own to flip the parent from profit to loss even before tax. Tax expense (a credit both periods) fell from 9,313,817 to 4,877,556 (-47%), a smaller offsetting benefit than in the prior year, so Profit for the period also swung to a loss: (23,430,377) vs +25,362,455 PY (-192%). EPS (0.05) vs 0.12 PY (both basic/diluted, per doc p.5). Stored tax_expense=-4,877,556 (negative = credit, per profit_before_tax - tax_expense = profit_after_tax convention; matches the raw disclosed positive figure directly here since Company PBT and PAT are both already negative). Balance sheet differs from GROUP mainly in the 'Investments in subsidiaries' line (1,878,171,059, doc p.3) which GROUP does not carry (consolidated instead); Company Total Assets 4,240,787,190 vs GROUP 7,437,628,118 -- the parent is materially smaller than the consolidated group, consistent with most generation assets sitting in subsidiaries. short_term_borrowings=1,392,214,658 (1,087,761,452 current interest-bearing loans + 304,453,206 bank overdrafts); long_term_borrowings=1,547,703,581. trade_receivables=766,015,622, trade_payables=40,595,357 (combined Trade-and-other lines, same flag as GROUP). Cash flow (doc p.9): cash_from_operations=(25,517,827) (Company-level operating cash outflow, unlike the Group's positive 35,232,213 -- driven by a 53,515,892 increase in trade and other receivables at Company level vs a much smaller 15,884,464 increase at Group level, i.e. intercompany receivables grew faster than external Group receivables); capex=(53,255,147); cash_from_investing=(55,547,617), which also includes an 8,184,469 'Investments in Subsidiaries' cash outflow not present at Group level; cash_from_financing=(285,394,616). depreciation_amortization=11,558,233 (11,543,934 Depreciation + 14,299 Depreciation of ROU Asset, per CF statement).

Source: Resus Energy PLC interim FS for the 3 months ended 30 Jun 2026 (unaudited/provisional, subject to audit, signed 12 Aug 2026). Statement of Financial Position - Group doc p.2, Statement of Profit or Loss - Group doc p.4, Statement of Cash Flow - Group doc p.8, Operating Segment Information doc p.10, Explanatory Notes doc p.11, Share Information doc p.12. NOTE: the document's own header is self-inconsistent -- the cover (doc p.1) reads "01st Quarter 2026-2027" while every internal statement page reads "Interim Financial Report 04th Quarter 2026-2027"; both are almost certainly template carry-over errors, since the actual reporting period is unambiguous from the column headers ('3 Months Ended 30th June', 30.06.2026 vs 31.03.2026 BS dates) -- this is Q1 of FY Apr2026-Mar2027, the quarter ended 30 Jun 2026, first-ever financial_statements entry for HPWR. Figures are in whole Rupees -- unit_scale='1'. Revenue from contracts with customers fell 28% (266,171,356 vs 369,254,914 PY); Direct costs fell only 20% (100,577,141 vs 126,361,727), so Gross Profit fell 32% (165,594,214 vs 242,893,187). Administrative expenses rose 9% (30,952,500 vs 28,504,026) and Other Operating Income of 6,516,502 PY did not recur (nil this quarter), so Results from operating activities fell 39% (134,641,715 vs 220,905,663). SEGMENTAL DRIVER (doc p.10, Hydro Power / Solar Power / Other): the Hydro Power segment is the dominant driver of the decline -- Hydro revenue fell 36.3% (141,335,510 vs 221,805,509 PY) and Hydro segment PBT swung from a Rs86,351,863 PROFIT in the prior-year quarter to a Rs12,063,769 LOSS this quarter (a Rs98.4Mn negative swing), driven by both the revenue decline and higher segment finance cost (93,770,449 vs 74,031,305, +26.7%). Solar Power segment was comparatively resilient: revenue -5.2% (79,597,747 vs 83,996,407) and segment PBT -4.3% (34,583,449 vs 36,133,086). The 'Other' segment PBT rose sharply (6,430,906 vs 328,790) but is small in absolute terms. GAP: the report's explanatory notes (doc p.11) do not include any rainfall/hydrology commentary explaining the Hydro segment's profit-to-loss swing, despite hydro being weather-dependent generation -- this is inferred purely from the segmental revenue/PBT numbers, not from management narrative, and is flagged as a genuine disclosure gap. GAP -- FX: despite HPWR being a power generator with debentures/interest-bearing borrowings, this interim report contains NO separate foreign-exchange gain/loss line anywhere in the P&L, segment note, or explanatory notes (contrast KCAB/LPL, which both carry an explicit FX line); Note 5 (doc p.11) confirms the one Rs403,290,000 debenture outstanding (Type B, issued 30 Mar 2022) carries a floating LKR rate (AWPLR +2.25%) with LKR issue/spot values -- no evidence of foreign-currency-denominated debt or fuel costs was found in this filing. Finance income rose sharply (5,908,996 vs 232,111 PY, +2,446%) and finance cost rose 14% (111,600,127 vs 98,324,037) -- neither is attributed to FX in the source; both are used at face value. Profit before tax fell 76% (28,950,586 vs 122,813,737). Tax expense swung from a Rs16,117,728 CHARGE (PY) to a Rs9,098,622 CREDIT/reversal this quarter (a favourable Rs25.2Mn swing) -- consistent with the reduction in Deferred tax liabilities from 260,490,323 (31 Mar 2026) to 248,878,686 (30 Jun 2026) on the BS -- this tax credit is the second-most-important driver cushioning PAT against the operating decline: PBT -76% but PAT only -64% (38,049,208 vs 106,696,009) because of it. Stored tax_expense=-9,098,622 (negative = credit, per profit_before_tax - tax_expense = profit_after_tax convention). EPS/SHARE COUNT: No of ordinary shares (doc p.12, Share Information) is 430,924,135 as at 30 Jun 2026, versus 86,184,827 a year earlier (30 Jun 2025) -- exactly 5.0x. The Statement of Changes in Equity (doc p.6) shows Stated Capital UNCHANGED at 967,483,260 across the whole of Q1 FY26/27 (1 Apr 2026 to 30 Jun 2026), meaning no new capital was raised during this quarter -- the 5x share-count increase must have occurred earlier, in FY2025/26, most likely a share sub-division (consistent with unchanged total stated- capital value alongside a 5x share-count jump). This is confirmed indirectly by EPS: Group EPS of 0.09 (2026) reconciles as 38,049,208/430,924,135=0.0883->0.09, and the PY comparative EPS of 0.25 reconciles as 106,696,009/430,924,135=0.2476->0.25 -- i.e. BOTH periods' EPS use the CURRENT 430,924,135 share count (the standard LKAS 33 treatment for retrospective restatement after a share split/subdivision). GAP: the explanatory notes (doc p.11) do not explicitly disclose a share sub-division/split by name -- this is inferred from the numbers alone and flagged as a disclosure gap. shares_in_issue=430,924,135 (current, per Share Information doc p.12) used throughout. NOTE: the BS 'Net assets per share' figures printed on doc p.2 (5.67 for 30.06.2026, 27.90 for 31.03.2026) do NOT reconcile against Total Equity / 430,924,135 shares (would give ~6.11 and ~6.02) nor against the old 86,184,827 share count (~30.55 and ~30.11) -- flagged as an unreconciled/likely-erroneous printed figure and NOT used for any stored field. Balance sheet (doc p.2): short_term_borrowings=1,749,458,300 combines current Interest bearing loans and borrowings (1,361,253,088) with Bank overdrafts (388,205,212); excludes current Lease liability (3,690,270), kept separate. long_term_borrowings=2,633,925,868 (non-current interest bearing loans and borrowings only; excludes non-current Lease liability, Retirement benefit obligations and Deferred tax liabilities). trade_receivables=624,096,954 and trade_payables=74,364,023 are the combined 'Trade and other receivables/payables' lines (not split into pure-trade vs other) -- flagged as combined. Cash flow (doc p.8): cash_from_operations=35,232,213; capex=(147,941,951) ('(Acquisition)/Reversals of property, plant and equipment'); cash_from_investing=(142,032,954); cash_from_financing=(301,533,636), driven by a Rs514,000,000 Commercial Paper issuance offset by Rs600,000,000 CP repayment and a Rs215,533,636 capital repayment of interest-bearing borrowing -- net financing outflow despite the large gross CP proceeds. depreciation_amortization=40,925,675 (Depreciation only, per CF statement; Depreciation of ROU assets is nil this period vs 465,702 PY).

interim_updates.note_text: Resus Energy PLC (HPWR) reported Group Revenue from contracts with customers of Rs.266,171,356 for Q1 FY2026/27 (quarter ended 30 June 2026), -28% YoY (2025: Rs.369,254,914). SEGMENTAL DRIVER (Operating Segment Information, doc p.10, Hydro Power / Solar Power / Other): the Hydro Power segment is the dominant driver of the decline -- Hydro revenue fell 36.3% to Rs.141,335,510 (2025: Rs.221,805,509) and Hydro segment PBT swung from a Rs.86,351,863 PROFIT in the prior-year quarter to a Rs.12,063,769 LOSS this quarter (a Rs.98.4mn negative swing), driven by both the revenue decline and higher segment finance cost (Rs.93,770,449 vs Rs.74,031,305, +26.7%). By contrast the Solar Power segment was comparatively resilient: revenue -5.2% (Rs.79,597,747 vs Rs.83,996,407) and segment PBT -4.3% (Rs.34,583,449 vs Rs.36,133,086). Direct costs fell only 20% (Rs.100,577,141 vs Rs.126,361,727), so Gross Profit fell 32% to Rs.165,594,214 (2025: Rs.242,893,187); Administrative expenses rose 9% (Rs.30,952,500 vs Rs.28,504,026) and a Rs.6,516,502 PY Other Operating Income item did not recur, so Results from operating activities fell 39% to Rs.134,641,715 (2025: Rs.220,905,663). Profit before tax fell 76% to Rs.28,950,586 (2025: Rs.122,813,737). Tax expense swung from a Rs.16,117,728 CHARGE (PY) to a Rs.9,098,622 CREDIT/reversal this quarter (a favourable Rs.25.22mn swing), consistent with the reduction in Deferred tax liabilities from Rs.260,490,323 (31 Mar 2026) to Rs.248,878,686 (30 Jun 2026) -- this tax credit is the second-most-important driver cushioning PAT against the operating decline: PBT -76% but PAT only -64% to Rs.38,049,208 (2025: Rs.106,696,009). No foreign-exchange gain/loss line is disclosed anywhere in this filing's P&L, segment note or explanatory notes -- Note 5 (doc p.11) confirms HPWR's one Rs.403,290,000 debenture outstanding carries a floating LKR rate (AWPLR +2.25%), with no evidence of foreign-currency-denominated debt or fuel costs found; this contrasts with both KCAB and LPL, which each carry an explicit FX-gain/loss P&L line. EPS Rs.0.09 vs Rs.0.25 PY, both restated to the current 430,924,135 share count -- No of ordinary shares (doc p.12) is 430,924,135 as at 30 Jun 2026 versus 86,184,827 a year earlier (exactly 5.0x), with Stated Capital unchanged at Rs.967,483,260 across the quarter, indicating the increase is most likely a share sub-division that occurred earlier in FY2025/26 (not explicitly named as such in the notes).
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: this is HPWR's first financial_statements/interim_updates entry in this DB (no closer prior quarter has been collected). Genuine filing-level gaps: (1) no rainfall/hydrology commentary anywhere in the explanatory notes (doc p.11) explains the Hydro segment's Rs.98.4mn PBT swing from profit to loss, despite hydro being weather-dependent generation -- the segment driver above is inferred purely from segmental revenue/PBT numbers, not management narrative; (2) no foreign-exchange gain/loss line is disclosed at all in this filing (contrast KCAB/LPL, which both carry an explicit FX line) -- confirmed via Note 5 that the one outstanding debenture is LKR-denominated floating-rate, so this appears to be a genuine absence of FX exposure rather than an undisclosed gap, but is flagged since HPWR is a power generator where FX exposure is common in the sector; (3) the 5.0x share-count increase (86,184,827 to 430,924,135) is not explicitly named as a share sub-division in the notes -- inferred from the unchanged Stated Capital value alongside the share-count jump; (4) the Company (standalone parent) also swung from a Rs.16,048,638 PY profit to a Rs.(28,307,933) loss this quarter, a materially different and worse swing than the Group's, since the parent's finance costs rose 30% (Rs.62,732,695 vs Rs.48,338,342) versus the Group's 14% (Rs.111,600,127 vs Rs.98,324,037) -- the filing does not explain why the parent carries relatively more finance-cost pressure than the consolidated Group.
interim_updates.takeaway: HPWR's 76% PBT decline is a Hydro-specific story: the Hydro Power segment alone swung Rs.98.4mn from profit to loss on a 36.3% revenue fall and rising segment finance costs, while Solar held up much better (PBT -4.3%). Unlike hydro-power generation losses typically being attributed to poor rainfall, this filing gives no hydrology commentary, so the cause of the Hydro segment's revenue collapse (lower generation volumes vs. lower tariffs vs. plant availability) cannot be confirmed from the document alone and is worth following up on directly. A Rs.25.22mn favourable tax-credit swing meaningfully cushioned the bottom line, so PAT's -64% decline understates the -76% operating/PBT deterioration. Notably, HPWR carries no FX exposure disclosure at all (its one debenture is LKR floating-rate), which is a point of differentiation from sector peers KCAB and LPL, both of which have FX-sensitive balance sheets.

operational_highlights: Group Revenue Rs.266,171,356, -28% YoY (2025: Rs.369,254,914); Group Results from operating activities Rs.134,641,715, -39% YoY; Group PBT Rs.28,950,586, -76% YoY (2025: Rs.122,813,737); Group PAT Rs.38,049,208, -64% YoY (2025: Rs.106,696,009).

Hydro Power segment PBT swung from a Rs.86,351,863 PROFIT PY to a Rs.12,063,769 LOSS this quarter (a Rs.98.4mn negative swing) on a 36.3% revenue decline (Rs.141,335,510 vs Rs.221,805,509) plus a 26.7% rise in segment finance cost -- the dominant driver of the Group decline. Solar Power segment was comparatively resilient, revenue -5.2%, PBT -4.3%.
Tax expense swung from a Rs.16,117,728 charge PY to a Rs.9,098,622 credit this quarter (Rs.25.22mn favourable swing), cushioning PAT (-64%) against the steeper PBT decline (-76%).

No FX gain/loss line disclosed in this filing; the one outstanding Rs.403,290,000 debenture is confirmed LKR floating-rate (AWPLR +2.25%), unlike sector peers KCAB and LPL which carry explicit FX lines.

Share count rose 5.0x YoY (86,184,827 to 430,924,135) with Stated Capital unchanged, consistent with an (undisclosed-by-name) share sub-division; EPS Rs.0.09 vs Rs.0.25 PY, both restated to the current share count.
key_drivers: Hydro Power segment PBT swing of Rs.98.4mn (Rs.86,351,863 profit PY to Rs.12,063,769 loss), driven by a 36.3% Hydro revenue decline plus a 26.7% rise in Hydro segment finance cost, is the dominant driver of the Group's 76% PBT decline.

A Rs.25.22mn favourable tax swing (Rs.16,117,728 charge PY to Rs.9,098,622 credit this quarter, tied to a reduction in Deferred tax liabilities) is the second-most-important driver, cushioning PAT decline to -64% versus the steeper -76% PBT decline.
Solar Power segment's relative resilience (revenue -5.2%, PBT -4.3%) partially offset the Hydro collapse but was not large enough to prevent the overall decline.
